reader.requirement: At --std 85, the order in which WRITE statements execute while a sequential file is created (OPEN OUTPUT) is the order a later READ returns the records, for fixed and variable-length records; that order changes only when records are added at the end (OPEN EXTEND), and a new OPEN OUTPUT starts the relationship over.
reader.edition-search: grep Dialect|Edition|CobolVersion|Std in SequentialConnector.cs: none. The OUTPUT arm of OpenCore truncates (FileMode.Create) and restarts the shared ordinal mint at 0; WRITE appends to the writer stream in execution order; nothing reorders.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_02 covers fixed-length records, REWRITE in place and one EXTEND; not exercised: variable-length (RECORD VARYING / OCCURS DEPENDING ON) records, repeated EXTENDs, and a second OPEN OUTPUT re-creating the file

probes.expected: the creation order 30,10,20 (not key or collating order), then the EXTEND records in their WRITE order, each at its own length

probes.printed: OPT EXTEND ABSENT 05; after OPEN OUTPUT re-creates O and one EXTEND: O [NEW001] / O [NEW002]
probes.expected: a new creation establishes a new successor relationship; the earlier records are gone

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR12  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12

reader.notes: The OUTPUT arm truncates and the writer appends in statement order; variable-length frames keep order and length. The edition-dependent sharing arm (DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility) decides only when a buffered record is flushed, not its place in the file.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-126/src/rw13b.cob (run rw13b-001, --std 85): a fixed 4-byte sequential file F receives only PLAIN WRITEs (AAAA, BBBB, CCCC, DDDD) in OPEN OUTPUT; a WRITE F AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE exists in the program but is never executed (IF SW = 1). Read back: six records, '[LF AAA] 00 / [A LF BB] 00 / [BB LF C] 00 / [CCC LF] 00 / [DDDD] 00 / [LF + 3 spaces] 04', five of them never written; the file bytes are LF AAAA LF BBBB LF CCCC LF DDDD LF. Without the dead ADVANCING statement the same WRITEs read back as the four records (reader wrgr12). Probe rw12.cob (rw12-001): a file written AFTER ADVANCING 1 then EXTENDed reads back 7 misaligned records for 5 written. Same at --std 2023 (rw13b-002). Cause: SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite sets FileModel.WrittenWithAdvancing from ANY WRITE of the file in the program (kb/Work PB5201, a deliberate reading of §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16, OK cite 'automatic advancing will be provided by the implementor to act as if the user had specified AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE'), and SequentialConnector.IsRecordPrintStream then frames every record with a line feed that READ returns as record data. Reading: GR12 (OK §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR12 'The successor relationship of a sequential file is established by the order of execution of WRITE statements') ties the records a READ returns to the records the WRITEs released; here a READ returns records no WRITE released, decided by a statement that never executed. It is upheld only if a file subject to GR16 advancing is a print representation that need not read back, which the 1985 text neither says nor denies.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SequentialIoBinder.cs#BindWrite: sets FileModel.WrittenWithAdvancing from any WRITE ADVANCING of the file, executed or not, which turns every record of the file into a print line (not an edition switch)
src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#IsRecordPrintStream: selects the print-line framing that READ does not strip
refuter.corrected: If the reading holds: NONCONFORMING (wrong-answer, cause b, same at 2023): a sequential file written only by plain WRITEs does not read back as those records when the program also contains a WRITE ADVANCING of that file, even one never executed.
